decisive_items: Heart deviated the tracheobronchial tree to the right, compressed left bronchus, and occupied almost the entire left hemithorax
Decreased size of the cardiac allograft, relieved compression of left bronchus, improved expansion of left lung
Further size remodeling of the cardiac allograft and only mild residual compression of the left bronchus
response.rationale: Serial post-transplant CT shows an oversized cardiac allograft occupying the left hemithorax and compressing the left bronchus, with gradual graft remodeling and symptom relief. This directly indicates a pediatric heart transplantation complication, whereas the embolic stroke and LVAD history are antecedent context rather than the post-operative diagnosis.

rejected.why: LVAD implantation and echo monitoring are historical/supportive, but the post-transplant allograft findings contradict an active LVAD complication.
Embolic stroke is the presenting history, not the finding explained by serial post-transplant imaging.
The allograft appears, but no vasculopathy features are described; size remodeling and bronchial compression are not cardiac allograft vasculopathy.
Echo indices are monitoring tools; cardiomyopathy is not established and the LVAD/transplant context points to an allograft complication.
Too general; cardiac disease does not capture the specific post-transplant allograft complication.
Vascular disease is vague and unsupported by the post-transplant CT findings.
Bronchial compression is caused by the cardiac allograft, not by intrinsic respiratory disease.
Weight and height are anthropometric data only; no growth disorder is diagnosed.
Explains the embolic strokes and LVAD history but does not account for the post-transplant cardiac allograft and bronchial compression findings.
LVEF and LV mass monitoring do not establish primary left ventricular dysfunction; allograft remodeling is the key finding.
Pulmonary embolism is unsupported; emboli were cerebral and related to the LVAD history.
No evidence of left-sided heart hypoplasia is present.
